extracted.intended_audience: established researchers applying for Wellcome Discovery Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and application guidance for the Wellcome Discovery Award: funding for established researchers proposing bold, creative research to deliver significant shifts in understanding that could improve human health and wellbeing. Covers assessment criteria (proposal quality, researcher, environment), application stages, and funder principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver a significant shift in understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications should aim to deliver a significant shift in understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators look for work that changes how a topic is understood, not just incremental additions; this is a high-level impact expectation for the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a significant advance over existing methodologies, conceptual frameworks, tools or techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications should provide a significant advance over existing methodologies, conceptual frameworks, tools or techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should demonstrate clear improvements or innovations in methods, frameworks, tools or techniques compared with the current state of the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential to stimulate new and innovative research
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications should have the potential to stimulate new and innovative research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wellcome values work that opens new directions or enables follow-on research beyond the immediate project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of proposed approach
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed approach should be novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of novelty include developing and testing new concepts, methods or technologies, or combining existing ideas and approaches in a new way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research experience and track record
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment includes research experience and track record of the applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider prior accomplishments and evidence that the team can execute the proposed ambitious research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational background
rubrics_metrics.description: Educational background of the researchers is assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of the holistic view of capability and readiness to lead the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career stage and trajectory
rubrics_metrics.description: Career stage and trajectory are evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wellcome typically expects established researchers (often 7+ years post-first independent position) for Discovery Awards; reviewers consider how the applicant's career path and future trajectory align with the proposal's ambitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership in the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Leadership in the field is a criterion for assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of leadership (e.g., leading teams, setting agendas, community recognition) supports confidence in the applicant's ability to deliver the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated ability to deliver ambitious projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must demonstrate ability to deliver ambitious projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track record or evidence that the applicant can manage and complete high-risk, high-reward programmes is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of institutional environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment includes the quality of the institutional environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for strong institutional support, appropriate facilities, and an environment conducive to the project's success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and resources available
rubrics_metrics.description: Support and resources available to the project are evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes access to equipment, technical support, administrative infrastructure, and other material resources necessary to deliver the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborations are considered in the research environment assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality, relevance and strength of collaborations (internal and external) that enhance the project's feasibility and impact are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career development opportunities for team members
rubrics_metrics.description: Career development opportunities for team members are evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wellcome values environments that support development of junior researchers and broader team career progression as part of the project setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness and required components (Stage 1: Application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Full application must include a detailed research plan, track record of investigators, and environment description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should provide a comprehensive research plan and supporting materials that address proposal quality, investigator track record, and details on institutional environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: External review standards (Stage 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected applications are sent for external expert review; reviewers are chosen based on expertise (not seniority) and multiple independent reviews are obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect expert scrutiny of scientific merits; the funder uses multiple independent expert assessments to inform decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview assessment focus (Stage 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Shortlisted candidates are interviewed; interviews begin with a presentation and focus on questions and answers, with the panel assessing scientific depth, ambition, and ability to deliver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparation should prioritize clear presentation of scientific depth, the project's ambition and feasibility, and the applicant's capacity to deliver; anticipate detailed questioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final decision governance (Stage 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final funding decisions are made by the Discovery Research Decision Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board integrates application materials, external reviews, and interview outcomes to make funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Research requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome has a strong commitment to open access and requires data sharing; Wellcome is a DORA signatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should include plans for open access publication and data sharing in line with Wellcome policies and DORA principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: People-centered assessment principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome applies a holistic assessment of researchers; career disruption is considered fairly and diverse career paths are valued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should document career context (e.g., disruptions, non-traditional paths) and highlight diverse contributions; reviewers will interpret CVs and track records in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambition premium (risk-tolerant assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bold ideas are valued over incremental work; long-term vision is preferred over short-term deliverables and risk-taking is encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that are ambitious and potentially high-risk/high-reward are positively regarded; applicants should justify the long-term vision and accept higher uncertainty where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding scale and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery Awards provide up to £8 million over 8 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should align scope and budget with the expectation of substantial, long-term support and justify the requested resources accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: suitability for established researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitable for established researchers leading independent research programs; typically 7+ years post-first independent position (compared with Career Development Award target).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should self-assess eligibility based on career stage and consider the Career Development Award if earlier in independence; demonstrate independence and leadership for Discovery Award suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter alignment and priority areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery research can be in any area relevant to Wellcome's mission, with priority given to Mental Health, Infectious Disease, Climate and Health, and Discovery Research (basic biology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While cross-disciplinary applications are acceptable, alignment with Wellcome mission areas may strengthen a proposal; applicants outside priority areas should articulate relevance to Wellcome's mission.
